workstreams.title: Investigate the failing controller and protocol tier assertions
workstreams.body: # Investigate the failing controller and protocol tier assertions `npm run test:controllers` and `npm run test:protocol` both report failing assertions. Observed in passing on 2026-07-29 by agents running the tiers as a side-check during WS-62; the counts they reported were inconsistent with each other and none was verified, so treat the scale as unknown and measure it first. Collection is not the problem — 31 and 17 files respectively, unchanged. The leading hypothesis, untested: commit `f0d901e` (WS-53) changed controller behaviour that these suites assert against — the Layer PRP guard now tests read content rather than tier keys, the PRD precondition was hoisted out of the per-tier helpers in `execute.layer` and `test.layer` into the top-level cascade, and the `create.task.lists` PRD guard gained a `useLegacyPrp` gate. Those suites were written before that commit. It was flagged at the time that WS-53 was verified by lint and tsc only, with no behavioural test run, so this is the expected shape of that gap. Confirm or refute by running the controller tier at `10473da` and at `f0d901e` and diffing the failures.

workstreams.title: File the two deferred controller teardown behaviours as issues
workstreams.body: # File the two deferred controller teardown behaviours as issues New AK issue list in `akissuelists/2026-07-w4/`; report-only, no source change. (1) `lad.process.layers.controller.ts` places `closeClient()` in a `finally` inside the outer `try`, so a throw from `client.createClient()` skips cleanup entirely and orphans the `lad-config-*` temp dir — pinned by name-diffing the temp dir before and after in `backend/tests/integration/protocol/lad.process.layers.protocol.ts`. (2) Every controller flushes its error response from `catch` and only then awaits `closeClient()` in `finally`, so for roughly 115 ms after a 412 the opencode process and its temp dir are still live. Both were observed for the first time by the rung-3 protocol suite and are pinned there as current behaviour; filing was deferred at the time. Nothing leaks in (2) — the defect is that a caller treating the response as "everything is torn down" is wrong.

workstreams.body: # Fix the inverted live-test gate in `backend/.env` `backend/.env:117` sets `LAD_LIVE_TESTS=1`, and `.env` is loaded and expanded by `src/utils/env.bootstrap.ts`, which `src/server.ts` imports — so dotenv fills the variable in whenever the shell leaves it unset, and *not* setting the gate enables rung 4 rather than disabling it. `npm run test:e2e` therefore reaches a real model on a plain invocation, and the same hole defeats the gate in `backend/tests/e2e/utils/lad.opencode.client.live.ts` and `lad.controllers.live.ts`; it caused two unintended live runs this session before being diagnosed. workstreams.title: Define the manifest's purpose and its use across the service classes
workstreams.body: # Define the manifest's purpose and its use across the service classes The manifest (`lad-manifest.json`, written by `LADCreateUpdateManifestService` and read via `LADManifestModel`) is a newer idea that was never designed end to end: what it is for, who owns it, when it is detected versus reused, and how it should be passed between the service classes are all undecided, so each service improvises. Plan that properly, define the contract, then implement it across the services. Named must-fix, carried over from ISS-804 in IL-73 (the process-layers bug hunt) which was dropped as unactionable without this design: `LADProcessLayersService` runs manifest detection in Phase 0, then Phase 1's `LADDetectBriefTypeService` detects it all over again — a second full LLM tier-detection pass on every greenfield run. The orchestrator cannot hand its result over because `LADDetectBriefTypeService.create()` accepts only `(monorepoRoot, brief, client?)`, `detectBriefType()` takes no manifest or status, and both `monorepoStatus` and its internal manifest service are private with no setter. The design must give the manifest a way to be passed in, and this duplicate pass must be gone when the card closes.

workstreams.body: # Correct the stale testing-standard doc and purge its orphaned embedded copy Two pieces of documentation drift left by the LADOpenCodeClient jest→vitest migration. Consciously not filed as a defect during the conformance review — no shipping code produces a wrong result — so it sits here as doc accuracy plus a decision. (1) Re-check the "Current conformance" table in `backend/docs/TESTING_REFERENCE.md`, which maps each subject to the four rungs (1 unit, 2 contract, 3 protocol, 4 live), against where the suites actually sit on disk. workstreams.title: Investigate the uncovered service guards and their covered twins
workstreams.body: # Investigate the uncovered service guards and their covered twins WS-162's closing mutation check enumerated 48 live defensive guards across the service classes and applied 87 mutations; eight guards stayed GREEN when their condition was reverted, so no test covers them: `test.layer:404` (task-list-model throw), `test.layer:769` (stage-level `completedCount` skip), `test.layer:989` (empty stage set is not "complete"), `create.task.lists:348` (tier-absent guard in `read()`), `codebase.analysis:155` (debug-gated `deleteSession`), `perform.analysis:235` (`if (!analysis) throw`), `detect.brief.type:156` (`if (this.localClient) closeClient()`) and `execute.layer:359` (task-list-model throw). Four of the eight have a COVERED twin in a sibling service or a few lines away — `test.layer:404` against `test.layer:399`, `test.layer:769` against `execute.layer:756`, `test.layer:989` against `execute.layer:974`, and `create.task.lists:348` against `create.prps:1053` — which suggests those pairs have drifted apart rather than differing deliberately. This is investigation first: establish per guard whether the asymmetry is real source drift (a defect, belonging with WS-164) or merely a test gap, before anything is filed or any test is written. WS-162's stage was authorised to measure, not to author tests, which is why the gap was recorded and left open.
